## The daily digest pipeline

**Trigger.** There are two entry points that converge on the same job. `POST /api/cron/digest` (`src/app/api/cron/digest/route.ts`) is an HTTP endpoint guarded by `assertCronSecret` (checks an `x-taskflow-cron` header against `TASKFLOW_CRON_SECRET`) and simply calls `runDigestEmailJob(new Date())`. Separately, an in-process scheduler (`src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts`, `startScheduler`/`tick`, started from `src/instrumentation.ts`) ticks every 60 seconds and, per `CADENCE_MINUTES["digest-email"] = 60`, enqueues a `"digest-email"` job once an hour. The queue in `src/server/jobs/queue.ts` (`enqueue`/`drain`/`runHandler`) dequeues it and dynamically imports and calls the same `runDigestEmailJob(now)`, retrying up to `MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5` on failure. Either path lands in `src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts`, which is the real orchestrator.

**Which orgs are due.** `runDigestEmailJob` gets its candidate org list from `usageRepo.listOrgIdsForRollup(50)` in `src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts` — a helper actually built for the usage-rollup job, reused here, meaning an org only becomes a digest candidate once it has a row in `organizationUsage`, and only the 50 most-recently-measured orgs are considered per tick. For each candidate it loads the org via `orgRepo.findOrgById` and checks `shouldRunForOrg(org, now)`, also in `digest-email-job.ts`: it rejects archived orgs and otherwise compares `now.getUTCHours()` against the org's single configured `settings.digestHourUtc` (a plain UTC hour, not a timezone). It then checks the `digest_email` feature flag via `isEnabled` (`src/lib/feature-flags.ts`) with context from `buildFlagContext` (`src/server/services/feature-flag-service.ts`); the flag is defined in `src/config/feature-flags.ts` as requiring plan `growth` or higher (overridable per org). Orgs failing either check are skipped entirely for that run.

**Who inside the org is subscribed.** `digest-service.ts`'s `listDigestRecipients(orgId)` calls `listDigestSubscribers(orgId)` in `src/server/repositories/notification-preference-repository.ts`, which selects distinct users from `notificationPreferences` who have `digestOnly = true` on at least one notification kind. There's no single org-wide "digest enabled" toggle — subscription is inferred from per-notification-kind preferences (rows written via `upsertPreference` in the same repository).

**Assembling one person's digest.** For each recipient, `digest-service.ts`'s `buildDigest(orgId, recipientId, windowStart, windowEnd)` (window = `[now - 24h, now]`) re-checks org existence and the feature flag, then calls `notificationRepo.listUnreadSince(orgId, recipientId, windowStart)` (`src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts`), filtering for `readAt IS NULL` and `createdAt` in range, capped at `DIGEST_MAX_ENTRIES = 50` (`src/config/constants.ts`). So content comes from pre-aggregated unread notifications, not raw tasks/comments directly. `renderDigest` then calls `renderEmail("digest", …)` in `src/server/services/email-service.ts`, which — notably — is a generic fallback that dumps props into an HTML table, not the polished `DigestEmail` React component in `src/emails/digest-email.tsx` (that component and its renderer `src/emails/render.ts` are never invoked from the live path — dead code). `sendEmail` then just logs the send (no real mail transport). Afterward, `runDigestEmailJob` calls `notificationRepo.markRead` on every included notification, which both records "digested" state and prevents re-sending on a later run within the same window.

**When a subscribed person still gets nothing.** In execution order: (1) their org wasn't in the top-50 usage-rollup candidate batch that tick; (2) the org is archived or missing; (3) it isn't the org's configured UTC hour; (4) the org's plan doesn't include `digest_email` and no override is set; (5) `buildDigest` returns `null` because they have zero unread notifications in the 24h window (`MIN_ENTRIES = 1`) — the "quiet day" case; (6) their user record can't be found via `findUserById`; (7) any error during their per-recipient processing is caught, logged, and counted as failed without blocking others; (8) implicitly, since notifications get `markRead` after inclusion, a duplicate cron trigger in the same window finds nothing new to send (no explicit "already sent today" flag). There's no separate mute/snooze/rate-limit mechanism beyond these.
